theorem: Uniform density of scalar L-layer MPNNs on the realizable order-L DIDM quotient
quantifiers: For every L in N_0, every r>0, every continuous g on K=Gamma_L(BF_d^r), and every epsilon>0

trusted_foundation.statement: At depth zero the DIDM state is the base feature; a coordinate projection separates any two distinct feature vectors and is a zero-layer MPNN readout.
trusted_foundation.source: Definition in arXiv:2602.08785v1: depth-zero DIDM and MPNN recursion

trusted_foundation.statement: On a compact metric space, distinct finite regular Borel measures define distinct continuous linear functionals, so some continuous test has different integrals.
trusted_foundation.source: Rudin, Functional Analysis: Riesz representation and separation of regular Borel measures

trusted_foundation.statement: Induct on depth. Two unequal descriptors differ in the previous descriptor or in their neighbor measure. The first case uses the induction separator. In the second, Riesz supplies a continuous previous-depth test; uniform approximation by the induction algebra preserves a nonzero integral gap, and one message-integral/update layer realizes that separator. Applying the same measure-separation argument to the final node distribution and mean pooling separates unequal DIDMs.
trusted_foundation.source: Definition in arXiv:2602.08785v1: DIDM recursion and message/update/readout operations; the induction is reconstructed in this certificate

trusted_foundation.statement: A constant channel gives the unit; concatenating two same-depth networks gives sums; concatenation followed by a continuous multiplication readout gives products. Uniform limits preserve the algebra operations.
trusted_foundation.source: Standard: parallel composition of finite-dimensional message-passing channels

trusted_foundation.statement: The real Stone-Weierstrass theorem makes every unital point-separating subalgebra uniformly dense in C(K).
trusted_foundation.source: Standard: real Stone-Weierstrass theorem on compact Hausdorff spaces

trusted_foundation.statement: Membership of g in the uniform closure means that for every positive epsilon there is an L-layer scalar MPNN F with sup over K of |F-g| below epsilon.
trusted_foundation.source: Standard: definition of closure in the uniform norm

limitations: The certificate treats compactness of the realizable DIDM image as a hypothesis because Claim 4's compactness clause was not contradicted; it independently reconstructs separation and density and does not assume the paper's Theorem E.12 or M.1. Its trusted boundary is Riesz representation and real Stone-Weierstrass.
